description.narrative: The project aligns with Oxfam's two-year response plan, focusing on a multi-sectoral approach encompassing WASH, Food and Economic Security, Protection, and Shelter. The proposed activities will enhance Oxfam's WASH response, integral to our goals and objectives.The project will be implemented by promoting the agenda of localization by developing the partnership with 2 local partners (PEF and CMWU) who are already collaborating with us on ongoing projects. Given Oxfam's ongoing response and numerous requests for assistance, we seek UNICEF’s support to provide a comprehensive WASH package targeting 1,000,000 (250,000 Men, 260,000 Women, 240,000 Boys, 260,000 Girls) in needs IDPs and host communities in the current IDPs sites and other new sites based onthe ongoing Oxfam IDPs sitesneed assessment in Khanyounis, Middle area and North Gaza. The proposed project will adopt the following approach to achieve expected results. The project will aim to achieve Improved access to water services (Output 1), byrepairing and quick fixing of water infrastructures to enhance water access (Activity 1.1); and providing water testing kits and chlorine for regular water quality testing and treatment to enhance water quality surveillance capacity (Activity 1.2). Secondly, this action will support Improved access to sanitation facilities and services at the community and makeshift IDP sites at South and North Gaza Strip (Output 2), by providing and installing shared emergency latrines at HH levels (Activity 2.1); supporting the community based solid waste management at Makeshift IDP camps using CfW approach (Activity 2.2), repairing and quick fixing of waste water infrastructures to improve sanitation services (Activity 2.3), and desludging of latrines in makeshift IDP sites as a part of fecal sludge management through operationalizing one desludging truck (8m3 or 23m3 based on actual need) during the implementation period for 20 days (Activity 2.4). Thirdly, this action will aim to achieve improved Access to BasicWater and Sanitation Services (Output 3), by providing of safe drinking waterto informal IDP populations and governomental schools (Activity 3.1); and supportging the operation of critical water and wastewater facilities (Activity 3.2). Fourthly, this action will support 1,000 IDPs families (6,000 individuals) within the informal IDPs sites with a public health promotion package to ensure increased resilience to public health risks (Output 4), by distributing emergency HKs and WASH NFI for 7 months including family hygiene kits, water storage buckets, MHM kits and dignity materials for most vulnerable individuals (people with disabilities or suffering with incontinence) utilizing UNICEF’s supply capacity (Activity 4.1); promoting hand washing through providing 194 emergency Hand Washing Stations as well as resourcing HWS with consumables (soap) (Activity 4.2); conducting IPC awareness at community level through providing hygiene promotion and providing IPC awareness at community levelon water borne diseases with adapted IEC materials through door to door sessions and community sessions, including distribution of key WASH IEC materials for the targeted population in line with the WASH Cluster’s Hygiene Promotion TWiG key IEC materials agreed for the Gaza response (Activity 4.3); and supporting community engagement mechanisms to increase acceptance, improve hygiene behaviorto mitigate WASH related disease and sustainability of communal WASH infrastructure (Activity 4.4), which includes identifying at least 12 Community Hygiene Promoters to support implementation of Public Health Promotion activities at community level with a rateof 1 CHP per 500 targeted people for 8 months. Finally, this action will also aim to achieve increased access to emergencyWASH service provision at 10 medical points and learning spaces (Output 5), by providing a minimum IPC package including repair and/or construction of water supply, latrines, hand washing stations <(>&<)> showers (Activity 5.1); and distributing WASH IPC materials for disinfection for three months (Activity 5.2)

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
